requirements: The paper 'Self-Expansion of Pre-trained Models with Mixture of Adapters for Continual Learning' has been reproduced

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that a ViT-B/16 model pretrained on ImageNet-1K can be loaded into memory

verification.spec: Load the ViT-B/16 model with ImageNet-1K pretrained weights (e.g., via timm 'vit_base_patch16_224' or HuggingFace 'google/vit-base-patch16-224') and confirm the model instantiates without error and has 12 transformer blocks with hidden dim 768.

sub_tasks.requirements: The datasets from Section 4.1 have been imported.
The train and test sets of CIFAR-100 are available

verification.spec: Confirm that CIFAR-100 train (50000) and test (10000) sets can be loaded (e.g., via torchvision.datasets.CIFAR100) with 100 classes accessible.

sub_tasks.requirements: The train and test sets of of ImageNet-R are available

verification.spec: Confirm that ImageNet-R train and test splits (200 classes, ~30000 images) can be loaded from disk with correct class labels.

sub_tasks.requirements: The train and test sets of ImageNet-A are available

verification.spec: Confirm that ImageNet-A train and test splits (200 classes, ~7500 images) can be loaded from disk with correct class labels.

sub_tasks.requirements: The train and test sets of VTAB are available. The VTAB dataset used is the VTAB subset from the ADAM paper; only five domains are used, and the domain order is fixed to "resisc45 10-19; dtd 20-29; pets 30-39; eurosat 40-49; flowers 50-59". Only 10 classes are selected and used for each domain; the numbers denote the class index of the 10 classes for each domain. For example, 10-19 denotes the 10th - 19th classes are in resisc are used. The original resisc contains 45 classes.

verification.spec: Confirm the VTAB subset from the ADAM paper is available with the fixed domain order resisc45 (classes 10-19), dtd (20-29), pets (30-39), eurosat (40-49), flowers (50-59), each with 10 classes, totaling 50 classes across 5 tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: Datasets (CIFAR-100, ImageNet_R, ImageNet-A) are split in a manner where each task/domain consists of 10 distinct classes

verification.spec: Load the CIL data loaders for CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-A and assert that each task's class label set has exactly 10 distinct classes and that all classes across tasks are disjoint.

sub_tasks.requirements: The LoRA, Convpass and ADAM adapters are available
The LoRA adapter can be applied (it is either implemented or an existing implementation is imported)

verification.spec: Import the LoRA adapter class/module in the codebase, instantiate it (e.g., LoRA(dim=768, r=8)) and run a forward pass on a random tensor of shape [B, N, 768]; verify the output shape matches the input and that only the low-rank matrices are trainable.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Convpass adapter architecture has been implemented from https://github.com/JieShibo/PETL-ViT/blob/main/convpass/vtab/convpass.py and can be selected as the functional adapter

verification.spec: Import the Convpass adapter class and confirm its implementation matches the reference at https://github.com/JieShibo/PETL-ViT/blob/main/convpass/vtab/convpass.py (contains convolutional bypass with the same layer structure). Instantiate it and run a forward pass on a dummy [B, N, d] tensor; verify output shape equals input shape and it can be selected as the functional adapter in SEMA configuration.

sub_tasks.requirements: The ADAM "adapter" is implemented from https://github.com/ShoufaChen/AdaptFormer/blob/main/models/adapter.py

verification.spec: Import the ADAM adapter module; verify it matches the AdaptFormer adapter implementation (down-projection linear, ReLU, up-projection linear, added as a side branch to the MLP). Instantiate with d=768, r=48 and run a forward pass; check that output shape equals input shape and confirm the layer names/structure follow the AdaptFormer reference.

sub_tasks.requirements: The architecture and training loop of SEMA have been implemented correctly, as in Section 3.
The architecture of SEMA has been implemented correctly.
The functional adapter, representation descriptor, and router have been implemented correctly
The functional adapter has been implemented correctly as described in Section 3.3, as a learnable down projection layer, then a ReLU function, then a learnable up projection layer

verification.spec: Inspect the functional adapter module and verify it is composed of a linear down-projection (d -> r), ReLU nonlinearity, and linear up-projection (r -> d), matching Eq. 1. Instantiate the module and confirm the sequence of operations via named children/parameters.

sub_tasks.requirements: The representation descriptor is implemented as an autoencoder with an encoder, non-linearity, then decoder
The encoder of the representation descriptor is implemented as a linear layer that projects to 128 dimensions

verification.spec: Inspect the encoder submodule of the representation descriptor (AE) and confirm it is a single linear layer projecting the input feature dimension (768 for ViT-B/16) to 128 dimensions.

sub_tasks.requirements: LeakyReLU is applied to the output of the encoder of the representation descriptor

verification.spec: Feed a tensor with both positive and negative values through the representation descriptor's encoder pipeline and verify that a LeakyReLU activation is applied after the linear encoder layer (e.g., negative outputs are scaled by a small slope rather than zeroed).

sub_tasks.requirements: The decoder of the representation descriptor is implemented as a linear layer that projects from 128 dimensions back to the original dimensionality

verification.spec: Inspect the decoder submodule of the representation descriptor and confirm it is a single linear layer mapping from 128 dimensions back to the input feature dimension (e.g., 768 for ViT-B/16).

sub_tasks.requirements: The router has been implemented as a linear mapping function (using a learnable matrix) followed by a softmax operation

verification.spec: Instantiate the router with K adapters, pass a random feature vector of dimension d, and check the output has shape K, sums to ~1.0, and all entries lie in [0, 1] — consistent with softmax(x @ W_mix).

sub_tasks.requirements: The functional adapter, representation descriptor and router have been correctly integrated into a transformer layer

The output of the second normalization layer (after the first normalization layer, then multi-head self-attention, then residual connection) is used as input for the representation descriptors, functional adapters, and router

verification.spec: Instrument a SEMA transformer block: run a forward pass with a hooked input, and verify that the tensor fed to representation descriptors, functional adapters, and the router at layer l is the output of the second LayerNorm (i.e., LN2 applied after MHSA + residual), and NOT the raw MHSA output or the MLP output. Compare captured tensor identity/shape with LN2 output.

sub_tasks.requirements: A linear combination of the outputs of the functional adapters is computed, with the weights corresponding to the output of the router

verification.spec: Construct a layer with K>1 mock functional adapters (returning known distinct outputs) and a router that outputs known weights w. Run a forward pass and verify the MLP-side output equals MLP(x) + sum_k w_k * f_k(x) as in Eq. 3.

sub_tasks.requirements: A linear combination of the outputs of the functional adapters is added to the output of the fully connected layer and the residual layer in the transformer block to produce the output for the transformer layer

verification.spec: Run a forward pass through a SEMA transformer block with K>1 adapters at that layer. Verify numerically that x_out == MLP(x) + sum_k w_k * f_k(x) + residual, where w_k are the router softmax weights. Compare to manually computed sum.

sub_tasks.requirements: The training loop of SEMA has been implemented correctly.
When training SEMA, the parameters of the pretrained model (e.g. ViT) are frozen.

verification.spec: Build a SEMA model and assert requires_grad=False for all parameters of the pretrained ViT backbone (patch embed, MHSA, MLP, LayerNorm), while adapter, router, and representation descriptor parameters have requires_grad=True.

sub_tasks.requirements: When training SEMA, the running statistics of the mean and standard deviation of the reconstruction error are stored for each representation descriptor, using the previous 500 samples (over all tasks) that were used for training prior to the current sample

verification.spec: Train SEMA for a synthetic task, feeding a known stream of samples; inspect the running mean mu and std sigma stored per representation descriptor and verify they match the mean/std of the reconstruction errors over the most recent 500 training samples (windowed statistics), not all samples ever seen.

sub_tasks.requirements: When training SEMA, the z-score corresponding to the $k$-th representation descriptor in layer $l$ can be computed as $z_k^l = (r_k^l - u_k^l)/\sigma_k^l$, where $r_k^l$ is the reconstruction error of the current input, $u_k^l$ is the associated running mean of the representation descriptor, and $\sigma_k^l$ is the associated running standard deviation of the representation descriptor

verification.spec: Set a representation descriptor's running mean mu and std sigma to known values, feed an input with a known reconstruction error r, and check the z-score computed by the codebase equals (r - mu) / sigma within numerical tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: When a new task is added, the classification head has been expanded to handle the new classes

verification.spec: Simulate arrival of task t+1 with new classes: check that the classification head's output dimension grows to include the new classes, and that the newly added output rows are trainable while previous rows can be preserved as configured. Verify head.out_features increases by |Y_{t+1}|.

sub_tasks.requirements: When training SEMA, the training loss and its components including the cross-entropy loss and the reconstruction loss have been implemented correctly, as defined in Section 3.
For training SEMA, the loss of the model $F$ is implemented correctly; given an input-label pair $(x, y)$, the cross entropy loss between the output of the model $F(x)$ and $y$ is computed

verification.spec: Run one training step on a batch (x, y) and confirm the classification loss equals torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(F(x), y) numerically (up to a small tolerance) by manually recomputing it and comparing.

sub_tasks.requirements: For training SEMA, the reconstruction loss for the representation descriptors is implemented correctly; given an input $x$ to the representation descriptor $g$, the loss is computed as the 2-norm of the difference between the input and output; $||x - g(x)||_2^2$

verification.spec: For an RD g, feed a fixed input x, obtain reconstruction g(x), and verify the reconstruction loss returned by the codebase equals sum((x - g(x))**2) (squared L2 norm) as in Eq. 2, within numerical tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: For training SEMA, the overall loss given an input-label pair $(x, y)$ is computed as the cross-entropy loss of the output of the network with the label $y$ and the sum of reconstruction losses of all representation descriptors across all layers

verification.spec: For a single (x, y) pair passed through SEMA, decompose the returned loss and confirm it equals CrossEntropy(F(x), y) + sum over all layers l and all k of RD_reconstruction_loss(g_{phi_k^l}(x^l)), matching Eq. 4.

The Finetune Adapter baseline has been implemented
The Finetune Adapter baseline is implemented by adding one SEMA adapter to each of all layers in the frozen ViT

verification.spec: Instantiate the Finetune Adapter baseline and verify that exactly one SEMA-style functional adapter (down/ReLU/up with r=48) is added at EVERY transformer layer of the frozen ViT (i.e., 12 adapters for ViT-B/16), and that no representation descriptors or expansion mechanism are present.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Finetune Adapter baseline is trained by continually fine-tuning the SEMA adapters throughout all tasks in the task stream encountered during training

verification.spec: Run the Finetune Adapter baseline over a 3-task toy CL stream and confirm that the same set of adapter parameters is updated during every task (no freezing between tasks, no addition of new adapters). Track parameter ids across tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: When training the Finetune Adapter baseline, the backbone ViT is frozen and only the (parameters of the) adapters are updated continually by all tasks

verification.spec: Inspect the Finetune Adapter training loop / optimizer's parameter groups and assert only adapter parameters are included, while all ViT backbone parameters have requires_grad=False across all tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: The accuracy formulas are implemented correctly as in Section B.3.

The average accuracy $A_N$ of all seen tasks after training on the $N$-th task, is computed as $A_N = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N A_{i,N}$, where $A_{i,N}$ is the accuracy of the $i$-th task after training on the $N$-th task

verification.spec: After training on the N-th task, call the evaluation routine and manually recompute A_N = (1/N) * sum_{i=1..N} A_{i,N} where A_{i,N} is the accuracy on the test split of task i using the model after training on task N. Confirm the returned metric matches the manual computation up to floating point tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: The average incremental accuracy $\bar{A}$ is computed as $\bar{A} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{t=1}^N A_t$, where $A_t$ is the average accuracy on all seen tasks after training on the $t$-th task

verification.spec: Verify the implementation computes average incremental accuracy as the mean of per-task-step accuracies: after training on each task t, compute A_t (average accuracy across all tasks seen so far on their test splits), and report A_bar = (1/N) * sum_{t=1}^N A_t. Test with a stub returning known A_t values and confirm the returned scalar matches the arithmetic mean.

sub_tasks.requirements: Method components (from critique splits and additions)

Code has been implemented such that when a new task arrives, the first epoch is used to scan input features through existing representation descriptors WITHOUT applying any gradient updates to the model (functional adapters, router, or RDs), and only after scanning is the expansion decision made

verification.spec: Instrument the training loop: at the start of each new task, verify that during the scanning pass optimizer.step() is NOT called and no learnable parameter values change (compare parameter tensors before and after the scanning epoch). Confirm the expansion decision is made based on aggregated z-scores from this scan. Assert equality of parameter tensors before/after scan.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that at each layer l, the expansion signal is triggered if and only if ALL existing representation descriptors at that layer report a z-score above the threshold for the incoming sample/task; i.e., expansion uses an AND (all-must-exceed) rule across existing RDs, not an OR rule

verification.spec: Unit test the expansion-decision function at a single layer: construct 3 mock RDs with configurable z-scores. Case A: z-scores [3.0, 3.0, 3.0] with threshold 2.0 -> expect expansion signal True. Case B: [3.0, 3.0, 0.5] with threshold 2.0 -> expect False (at least one RD covers). Case C: [0.5, 0.5, 0.5] -> expect False. Assert all three cases match expected outputs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that during a new task, at most one adapter is added per transformer layer (task-oriented expansion constraint enforced regardless of intra-task variation)

verification.spec: Instantiate the SEMA model with self-expansion enabled on the last three ViT blocks. Simulate one task by feeding a batch of features that would repeatedly trigger the z-score threshold at layer L. Record adapter count K^L before and after the task's first-epoch scan. Assert that K^L increases by at most 1 per layer for this task, even after many triggering batches.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that when an adapter is added at layer l during first-epoch scanning, the model completes training on the current task at that layer before scanning proceeds to deeper layers

verification.spec: Run one CL task with expansion enabled on layers L-2, L-1, L. Instrument the training loop to log the sequence of (layer_index, event) events where event in {'scan','add','train','scan_next'}. Assert that whenever an 'add' happens at layer l, a 'train' event for that layer precedes any 'scan' event at layer l+1 for that task.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that self-expansion scanning at each new task proceeds sequentially from shallow to deep transformer layers

verification.spec: Import the self-expansion loop and inspect the iteration order of layers considered for expansion. Assert that the iterable of layer indices is sorted ascending (shallow -> deep), matching the description in Section 3.6.
